games.title: Change Blindness
games.subtitle: Spot the single item that changes between flashes.
games.objective: Identify the single difference between two alternating images before the time runs out.
games.controls: Tap the area on the image where you spot the change.
walkthrough: Step 1: The screen flashes between two nearly identical images.
Step 2: Carefully scan the images to spot what appears or disappears.
Step 3: Tap the changed region.
Step 4: Find the changes across multiple rounds to win.
strategies: Keep your eyes focused on one section of the image at a time.
Look for objects that suddenly appear or disappear.
Do not tap randomly, as incorrect taps may penalize you.

games.title: Colour Match
games.subtitle: Tune the sliders to match the target colour.
games.objective: Determine if the meaning of the word matches the ink color it is written in.
games.controls: Tap '''Yes''' if it matches, or '''No''' if it doesn'''t.
walkthrough: Step 1: A word describing a color appears on screen.
Step 2: Look at the actual color of the text.
Step 3: Decide if the word text matches the color.
Step 4: Answer quickly and accurately across multiple trials.
strategies: Focus primarily on the visual color first, then read the word.
Try to disconnect your reading brain from your visual processing.
Don'''t rush too fast, as errors cost points.

games.title: Schulte Table
games.subtitle: Tap the numbers in order from 1 to 25.
games.objective: Find and tap all the numbers in the grid in ascending order as fast as possible.
games.controls: Tap the numbers on the grid in order, starting from 1.
walkthrough: Step 1: A 5x5 grid of randomly placed numbers (1-25) is presented.
Step 2: Find and tap the number 1.
Step 3: Continue finding and tapping the numbers in ascending order (2, 3, 4...).
Step 4: Complete the grid in the shortest time possible.
strategies: Keep your eyes focused on the center of the grid.
Use your peripheral vision to locate the next numbers.
Try to spot the next number while moving your finger to the current one.

games.title: Shell Game
games.subtitle: Track the hidden ball while the cups swap places.
games.objective: Keep your eye on the container hiding the target object as they are rapidly shuffled.
games.controls: Tap the container you believe holds the target object once they stop moving.
walkthrough: Step 1: Note which container holds the target object before they cover it.
Step 2: Follow that specific container with your eyes as they shuffle around.
Step 3: Do not let distractor containers break your focus.
Step 4: Tap the correct container when the shuffling stops.
strategies: Fixate your eyes between the target container and the center of the screen.
Avoid blinking during fast shuffles.
If tracking multiple targets, expand your visual focus rather than darting your eyes.

games.title: Visual Search
games.subtitle: Find the unique symbol in the grid
games.objective: Find the unique target symbol among a dense array of similar distractors.
games.controls: Tap the target symbol in the grid.
walkthrough: Step 1: Read the target description or symbol layout to look for.
Step 2: Scan the grid of distractors rapidly.
Step 3: Locate the unique target item.
Step 4: Tap it to score and advance.
strategies: Scan in a systematic grid path (e.g. left-to-right rows) instead of random looking.
Look for features that stand out (such as line orientation or color).
If the target has a distinct feature, look for that specific difference.

games.title: Akari
games.subtitle: Illuminate all white cells
games.objective: Place lightbulbs to illuminate every empty cell in the grid without any two lightbulbs shining on each other.
games.controls: Tap an empty cell to place a lightbulb. Tap a placed lightbulb to remove it.
walkthrough: Step 1: Look for black cells with numbers. The number indicates exactly how many lightbulbs must be placed adjacent (top, bottom, left, right) to that cell.
Step 2: Place lightbulbs around numbered cells where the placement is forced (e.g., a '4' needs a bulb on all four sides).
Step 3: Lightbulbs illuminate their entire row and column up to the grid edge or a black cell block.
Step 4: Ensure no two lightbulbs illuminate each other.
Step 5: Continue placing bulbs until every empty white cell is illuminated.
strategies: Start with the highest numbers ('4' or '3') as they often have limited or forced placement options.
If a '0' block is on the grid, you know no bulbs can be placed adjacent to it.
Look for isolated cells that can only be illuminated by a bulb placed in that exact spot or row/column.

games.title: Binary Puzzle
games.subtitle: Fill 0s and 1s equally with no three in a row.
games.objective: Fill the grid with 0s and 1s such that no three identical numbers are adjacent, each row and column has an equal number of 0s and 1s, and all rows and columns are unique.
games.controls: Tap an empty or modifiable cell to toggle its value between empty, 0, and 1.
walkthrough: Step 1: Examine the grid for fixed starting numbers.
Step 2: Look for pairs of identical numbers (e.g., '1-1'). The cells on either side must be the opposite number (e.g., '0-1-1-0').
Step 3: Look for identical numbers separated by one empty cell (e.g., '1-_-1'). The empty cell must be the opposite number ('1-0-1').
Step 4: Ensure every row and column contains exactly half 0s and half 1s.
Step 5: Ensure no two rows are identical and no two columns are identical.
Step 6: Continue deducing cell values until the grid is filled correctly.
strategies: If a row or column has reached its maximum quota of 1s, fill the remaining empty cells with 0s.
Compare nearly completed rows or columns with existing ones to avoid creating duplicate rows or columns.
Always apply the 'no three in a row' rule first, as it provides the most immediate deductions.

games.title: Block Escape
games.subtitle: Slide blocks to clear a path to the exit.
games.objective: Clear a path to slide the target block out of the exit on the right side of the board.
games.controls: Drag blocks along their horizontal or vertical axis to move them into empty spaces.
walkthrough: Step 1: Identify the distinct target block (usually colored differently) that needs to reach the exit on the right.
Step 2: Locate the blocks obstructing the target block's path to the exit.
Step 3: Drag the obstructing vertical and horizontal blocks out of the way to create a clear lane.
Step 4: Slide the target block through the exit to solve the puzzle.
strategies: Work backwards: look at the exit and determine which block is directly blocking it, then figure out how to move that specific block.
Horizontal blocks can only move left/right, and vertical blocks can only move up/down.
Sometimes you have to move a block into the target's path temporarily to shuffle other blocks around.

games.title: Boats
games.subtitle: Place the fleet to match the row and column counts.
games.objective: Place the whole fleet: every boat is a straight run of boat cells, no two boats touch even at a corner, and the counts outside the grid say how many boat cells each row and column holds.
games.controls: Tap a cell to cycle it through boat cell, water, and untouched. No dragging is needed.
walkthrough: Step 1: Read the numbers along the top and the left. A 0 empties that whole row or column, so tap every cell in it to water.
Step 2: Mark boat cells with the longest boat first. A run of four needs four cells in a line, so a line that cannot hold four anywhere is not part of it.
Step 3: Once a row or column has all the boat cells its count asks for, tap the rest of that line to water.
Step 4: Two boat cells that touch at a corner are a mistake even when both runs have the right length. Water one of them.
Step 5: The strip under the board crosses a boat off when you have marked a complete one. The board is finished when every boat is crossed off and the counts are met.
strategies: Whenever a cell has boat cells on both a row neighbour and a column neighbour, it cannot be a boat: a boat is a straight run, so it would have to bend.
A boat cell rules out all four cells diagonally beside it, not just the four it touches.
If a line's count is only just satisfied by the cells still open, every one of them is a boat.
Count the fleet, not just the lines: when the remaining lengths cannot fit in a gap, that gap is water.

games.title: Bricks
games.subtitle: Shade supported cells with no three in a row.
games.objective: Shade cells of the honeycomb so that every shaded cell stands on a shaded cell below it, no three shaded cells sit in a row, and every number counts the shaded cells around it.
games.controls: Tap a cell to shade it, and tap it again to clear it. A numbered cell is fixed: it counts its neighbours and is never shaded.
walkthrough: Step 1: Read the bottom row first. A shaded cell there needs nothing under it, so the bottom row is where a pile can start.
Step 2: A cell on any other row can only be shaded if one of the two cells under it, down-left or down-right and never straight down, is shaded. That pair is the whole rule this game is named after.

Step 3: Count for every number. A cell with as many shaded neighbours as its number is finished, and every neighbour still empty is unshaded. A number that needs every neighbour it has left shades them all.
Step 4: Watch the horizontal runs. Two shaded cells side by side forbid the third in that row, so a run of two is a wall you can lean on.

Step 5: Work a shaded cell downwards when you are stuck: it has to reach a shaded cell, so when only one of its two cells below is still open, that one is shaded. The board is finished when every shade is held up, no run reaches three, and every number reads true.
strategies: Start at the bottom and climb. A shade high up is only legal because of the cells under it, so a wrong cell at the top is usually a wrong cell two rows below.
A number of zero is the strongest clue on the board: its own cell is unshaded and so is every neighbour it counts, whichever way the pile leans.
Gravity and the run rule fight on the left and right edges, where a cell has only one neighbour below it: there the rule collapses into a single forced cell.
When two cells below a shade are both still open, leave them. The board only forces a cell when the count is tight or one of the pair is already ruled out.

games.title: Bridges
games.subtitle: Connect islands with bridges that match each count.
games.objective: Connect all islands into a single continuous network with bridges, ensuring each island has exactly the number of bridges indicated by its number.
games.controls: Tap an island to select it, then tap an adjacent island to draw a bridge. Tap again to upgrade to a double bridge, or tap a third time to remove the connection.
walkthrough: Step 1: Review the numbered islands on the grid.
Step 2: Tap an island to select it, then tap an orthogonal (up, down, left, right) island to connect them with a bridge.
Step 3: Bridges cannot cross other bridges or islands.
Step 4: Each island must have a total number of connected bridges equal to its number.
Step 5: All islands must be connected together in one single group to solve the puzzle.
strategies: Look for corners with '4', edges with '6', or center islands with '8'. These require double bridges in all available directions.
If a '1' island is connected, no other bridges can attach to it.
Ensure you don'''t create an isolated closed loop of islands; the network must be fully connected.

games.title: Clusters
games.subtitle: Two colours: dots touch one mate, others touch two.
games.objective: Colour every cell one of two colours, so that a dotted cell has exactly one neighbour of its colour and a cell without a dot has at least two.
games.controls: Tap a cell to cycle it: empty, then one colour, then the other, then empty again. A dotted cell is fixed and does not change.
walkthrough: Step 1: Read a dot as a small puzzle of its own. The dot already shows the colour of its cell, so that cell is done, and exactly one of its neighbours shares it.
Step 2: A corner cell without a dot has only two neighbours, so both of them must be its colour. That is the strongest start on the board.
Step 3: Count neighbours, not patterns. A cell needs two of its colour, so when one neighbour is the other colour and one is empty, the empty one is decided.
Step 4: A dotted cell with no same-coloured neighbour yet needs its one from the cells still open. When only one is open, that one takes the colour.
Step 5: The board is finished when every cell is coloured, every dot has exactly one neighbour of its colour, and every plain cell has two. A cell that cannot reach its count shows in red.
strategies: Work from the corners inward: a corner without a dot forces both of its neighbours, which then forces the next ring.
A dot with one neighbour already its colour rules out that colour for every other neighbour, which is often the fastest way to place an edge.
Two colours are symmetrical, so a mistake is not local: a cell that cannot reach two neighbours of its colour usually means the cell two steps away is wrong.
An edge cell has three neighbours, so it needs two of its own colour: one of the three is the odd one out, and the dot tells you which.

games.title: Color Flood
games.subtitle: Moves: /
games.objective: Flood the entire grid with a single color within the allowed number of moves.
games.controls: Tap the color buttons at the bottom to change the color of your growing cluster.
walkthrough: Step 1: Start from the top-left corner tile.
Step 2: Choose a color that matches adjacent tiles to absorb them.
Step 3: Continue changing colors to expand your area.
Step 4: Fill the entire board with one color before running out of moves.
strategies: Always pick the color that absorbs the maximum number of new tiles.
Look ahead to see which color will open up large sections.
Work towards the edges of the board.

games.title: Crowns
games.subtitle: One crown per row, column, and region; none touching.
games.objective: Place crowns on the grid so that no two share the same row, column, or colored region, and they don't touch diagonally.
games.controls: Tap empty cells to place or remove a crown. Long press to mark with an X.
walkthrough: Step 1: Analyze the colored regions on the grid.
Step 2: Place one crown in each region, row, and column.
Step 3: Ensure crowns do not touch even diagonally.
Step 4: Fill the necessary spots to solve the puzzle.
strategies: Start with small regions where placement options are limited.
Use the X marker to cross out invalid cells.
Remember that corners diagonally adjacent to a crown are invalid.

games.title: Cube
games.subtitle: Roll the cube to collect every blue square.
games.objective: Roll the cube over the board until all six of its faces are blue.
games.controls: Drag the cube onto a neighbouring square, or tap that square. There is no undo, but every roll can be rolled back by rolling again.
walkthrough: Step 1: Read the board first. A blue square paints the face the cube lands on; a white square unpaints one.
Step 2: Roll onto blue squares early, while most faces are still white.
Step 3: Watch the bottom face as you roll: it is the one that changes, and the other four edges rotate around it.
Step 4: Finish when all six faces are blue. The faces counter tracks how many are done.
strategies: Every roll swaps the bottom face with the square you land on, so a roll is its own inverse. If a roll makes things worse, roll back.
Plan a route that visits each blue square once rather than crossing the same square twice.
Work from a corner: a corner only has two exits, so it is the cheapest place to fix a face.

games.title: Dominosa
games.subtitle: Pair adjacent numbers so each domino appears once.
games.objective: Reconstruct a set of dominoes by pairing adjacent numbers on a grid.
games.controls: Tap and drag between adjacent numbers to form a domino.
walkthrough: Step 1: Look at the grid of numbers.
Step 2: Identify pairs of adjacent numbers that make up valid domino tiles.
Step 3: Tap and drag to group two numbers together.
Step 4: Cover the entire grid exactly once with no overlapping dominoes.
strategies: Look for pairs that can only be formed in one specific location.
Work from the edges and corners inward.
Keep track of which dominoes (e.g., 2-3, 4-4) you have already placed.

games.title: Fillomino
games.subtitle: Group cells into regions matching their number.
games.objective: Divide the grid into polyominoes of matching sizes. Two polyominoes of the same size cannot touch share an edge.
games.controls: Tap cells to cycle through numbers from 1 to 9.
walkthrough: Step 1: Examine the starting numbers on the grid.
Step 2: Each number represents the size of the block (polyomino) it belongs to.
Step 3: Tap adjacent cells to assign them the same number to group them.
Step 4: Ensure no two blocks of the same size share a horizontal or vertical edge.
Step 5: Fill all grid cells to solve the puzzle.
strategies: Start with small numbers like 1, which are immediately isolated blocks.
Look for paths that are forced to extend because they cannot merge with adjacent groups of the same size.
Keep track of block sizes by counting cells with the same number.

games.title: Four Colours
games.subtitle: Colour every region so touching regions never match.
games.objective: Colour every region with four colours so that no two regions that share a border share a colour. Any valid colouring wins.
games.controls: Tap a region to cycle its colour. A region that clashes with a neighbour glows red.
walkthrough: Step 1: Start with the region that has the most neighbours, and give it a colour.
Step 2: Colour its neighbours with the other colours, one at a time.
Step 3: Continue outward. A clash is shown immediately, so you can always see what is wrong.
Step 4: The board is done when every region has a colour and nothing glows.
strategies: Unlike the other puzzles here, this one has many answers on purpose: any valid four-colouring is correct.
Regions that touch at a corner are not neighbours. Only a shared border constrains the colour.
If you get stuck, pick the region with the fewest remaining colours and change it first.

games.title: Four Letters
games.subtitle: Place A, B, C, or D to match the edge counts.
games.objective: Write one letter in every cell so that each row and column holds exactly the number of each letter printed beside it, and no two identical letters touch along an edge.
games.controls: Tap a cell to cycle its letter: empty, then A, B, C, D, and back to empty. The hint button fills one cell the counts prove.
walkthrough: Step 1: Read one row's clue as four digits in alphabet order. On a five-cell row, `2111` means two As, one B, one C and one D.
Step 2: When a clue digit is met, that letter cannot appear again in the line. When the cells left in a line equal the counts still owed, those cells are fixed.
Step 3: Two identical letters may not share an edge, so a letter in a cell rules itself out of the cells above, below, left and right.
Step 4: Work the tightest line first: a line with a 0 or a line whose counts are almost used up is where the next certain letter is.
Step 5: The grid is finished when every cell holds a letter and every clue digit is met; a letter touching its twin is shown in red.
strategies: A row whose clue has a 0 removes that letter from the whole row at once.
If a letter's count in a line equals the number of free cells, every free cell of that line is that letter.
Alternate thinking: a run of cells that can hold a letter at most every other cell bounds that letter's count. When the bound equals the clue, the alternation is forced.
Column and row clues cross, so a letter forced in a row very often fixes a cell in a column too. Sweep both directions each time you place one.

games.title: Futoshiki
games.subtitle: Fill each row and column while obeying the signs.
games.objective: Fill the grid with numbers such that each row and column contains unique numbers, while respecting the inequality signs (<, >) between cells.
games.controls: Tap a cell to select it, then use the numpad at the bottom to enter a number. Use the erase button to clear a cell.
walkthrough: Step 1: Look for inequality signs between adjacent cells.
Step 2: Find rows or columns with missing numbers and use the signs to deduce the values.
Step 3: Tap an empty cell and select the correct number from the bottom row.
Step 4: Complete the grid without violating any inequality constraints or row/column uniqueness.
strategies: Look for chains of inequalities (e.g., A < B < C) which severely restrict possible numbers.
Identify the highest and lowest possible numbers in the grid to fill edges of inequalities.
Use the process of elimination in rows and columns as you would in Sudoku.

games.title: Galaxies
games.subtitle: Give every dot its own symmetric region
games.objective: Split the board into regions, one per dot. Every region must be symmetric about its own dot, and no region may hold two dots.
games.controls: Tap a dot to pick it up, then tap the cells that belong to it. Or drag the dot onto a cell. Painting a cell also paints the cell it reflects onto. Tap a painted cell with no dot picked to clear it. The hint button shows one cell the rules can prove.
walkthrough: Step 1: Tap a dot to pick it up. The dot you picked is ringed.
Step 2: Tap a cell near that dot. Its mirror image about the dot is painted at the same time, so the region stays symmetric.
Step 3: Keep painting outward until the region is as big as it can be without touching another dot's cells.
Step 4: Move to the next dot and repeat. The board is solved when every cell belongs to exactly one dot.
strategies: Start with the dots closest to an edge. Their regions have the fewest places to go, so they decide themselves quickly.
A cell whose mirror image is already another dot's cannot belong to this dot. That single fact usually settles the cells around a crowded corner.
Watch for cells that would be cut off. If painting a cell would leave a gap no region can reach, that cell belongs to the dot on the other side of the gap.
When two dots are close together, one of them usually has only one way out. Find it before painting anything else.

games.title: Gokigen Naname
games.subtitle: Draw diagonals to connect points without loops.
games.objective: Draw a diagonal line in every cell so that the lines meeting at each intersection match the number clue, without forming any closed loops.
games.controls: Tap a cell to toggle the direction of its diagonal line (forward slash or backslash).
walkthrough: Step 1: Look at the numbered circles at the grid intersections.
Step 2: A number indicates exactly how many diagonal lines must connect to that circle.
Step 3: Tap cells to draw diagonals, ensuring they satisfy all numbered intersections.
Step 4: Check that your lines do not create any closed loops.
strategies: Start with corners and edges; a '0' or '4' in the middle, or '0' or '2' on an edge, forces specific diagonals.
If a '1' is in a corner, only one line can connect to it.
Remember that loops are forbidden; if placing a line would close a loop, you must use the opposite diagonal.

games.title: Heyawake
games.subtitle: Shade grid rooms without adjacent black cells.
games.objective: Paint cells black or white in rectangular rooms according to numeric room constraints.
games.controls: Tap an empty cell once to paint black, tap twice to mark with a green dot.
walkthrough: Step 1: Check rooms with numbers; each specifies the exact count of black cells inside that room.
Step 2: Ensure no two black cells touch orthogonally.
Step 3: Keep all unshaded white cells connected into a single open path.
strategies: A room with '0' must have all white cells.
White corridors cannot span across more than two consecutive rooms in a straight line.

games.title: Hitori
games.subtitle: Shade duplicate numbers without splitting the grid.
games.objective: Shade duplicate numbers in the grid such that no row or column contains repeats among unshaded cells, black cells don't touch orthogonally, and unshaded cells remain connected.
games.controls: Tap a cell once to shade (black), tap twice to circle (safe).
walkthrough: Step 1: Locate rows and columns with duplicate numbers.
Step 2: Shade duplicates so only one instance remains visible.
Step 3: Ensure shaded cells are never orthogonally adjacent.
strategies: If a cell is shaded black, all four orthogonal neighbors must be unshaded (circle them).
Between two identical numbers with one cell in between, the middle cell must be unshaded.

games.title: House Logic
games.subtitle: Use the clues to deduce every house's traits.
games.objective: Use a set of clues to deduce the attributes belonging to different subjects on a grid.
games.controls: Tap grid cells to mark them as true (check) or false (cross) based on the clues.
walkthrough: Step 1: Read the list of available logical clues.
Step 2: Cross-reference attributes on the logic grid.
Step 3: Tap a cell to mark an intersection as true (which auto-crosses out the rest of the row/column).
Step 4: Continue deducing until the entire grid is correctly filled.
strategies: Start with the most direct clues that explicitly link two items.
Use negative clues to eliminate possibilities immediately.
Look for chain reactions where placing one checkmark forces another.

games.title: Inertia
games.subtitle: Slide the ball to collect every gem and miss mines.
games.objective: Collect every gem on the board without touching a mine.
games.controls: Drag the ball onto the square it would land on, or tap any square in line with it. The ball slides until a wall stops it and cannot stop halfway.
walkthrough: Step 1: Find the gems first and the mines second. A route between them is the puzzle.
Step 2: Move along one direction at a time. Each move ends against a wall, so it always changes your row or your column completely.
Step 3: Collect the gems one at a time, checking that the stop square is not a mine.
Step 4: The board is won when the last gem is collected.
strategies: A move always ends at a wall, so think in terms of which wall you want to end against.
Mines are only dangerous where you stop, not where you pass. Crossing a mine's row is safe.
Leave a gem near a dead end for last, so you always have somewhere to go.

games.title: Kakurasu Sums
games.subtitle: Shade cells to meet weighted row/col index sums.
games.objective: Shade cells in a grid so that the sum of the weights of the shaded cells matches the target sums for each row and column.
games.controls: Tap a cell to toggle its shaded state.
walkthrough: Step 1: Note the weights (1, 2, 3, 4...) located on the top and left edges of the grid.
Step 2: Check the target sums located on the right and bottom edges.
Step 3: Tap cells to shade them. A shaded cell in column 3 adds 3 to its row's sum.
Step 4: Continue shading until all row and column targets turn green.
strategies: Look for high target numbers that require almost all cells in a row/column to be shaded.
Look for low targets (like 1 or 2) where only one specific cell can be shaded.
Use cross-referencing: shading a cell affects both its row and column sum simultaneously.

games.title: Kakuro
games.subtitle: Fill digits that add up to each clue with no repeats.
games.objective: Fill the white cells with digits 1-9 so that the sum of each contiguous horizontal/vertical block matches its clue, without repeating any digit within a block.
games.controls: Tap a white cell to select it, then tap a number on the keypad to enter it. Use the backspace button to clear a cell.
walkthrough: Step 1: Find a clue block (number with a diagonal line).
Step 2: The top-right number is the target sum for the horizontal block to its right. The bottom-left is for the vertical block below it.
Step 3: Tap a white cell and use the keypad to enter a digit from 1 to 9.
Step 4: Ensure no digits repeat within a single sum block.
strategies: Learn common Kakuro combinations (e.g., a 2-cell sum of 3 must be 1+2; a 2-cell sum of 4 must be 1+3).
Look for intersections of restrictive sums (e.g., a low horizontal sum crossing a low vertical sum).
Use pencil marks or mental notes to track possible candidates for each cell.

games.title: Kurodoko
games.subtitle: Shade cells so numbers see that many white cells.
games.objective: Blacken cells until every numbered cell sees exactly as many white cells as its number says, counting across and down through itself.
games.controls: Tap a cell to blacken it, tap it again to mark it white, and a third time to clear it. Numbers cannot be changed.
walkthrough: Step 1: A number counts the white cells in an unbroken line through it, across plus down, with the cell itself counted once.
Step 2: Start with a clue whose number is larger than the room around it. The cells it must reach have to be white.
Step 3: When a clue already sees its number, the cells just past the line on both sides have to be black.
Step 4: Blacken a cell and its four neighbours are white. Keep the white cells in one connected group and the board falls.
strategies: A clue of 1 on a cell with neighbours means every neighbour is black.
Two black cells can never share an edge, so a black cell settles four cells at once.
If blackening a cell would cut the white cells into two groups, that cell has to be white.
When nothing else moves, try a cell one way and follow the consequences. If it contradicts, the other way is forced.

games.title: Lighthouses
games.subtitle: Place boats so each lighthouse sees its count.
games.objective: Place ships in the grid so that each lighthouse points to the correct number of ships in its row and column.
games.controls: Tap grid cells to place or remove ships.
walkthrough: Step 1: Look at the numbers on each lighthouse.
Step 2: Place ships in the same row or column as the lighthouse to match its number.
Step 3: Ensure ships do not touch each other or the lighthouses, even diagonally.
Step 4: Satisfy all lighthouse conditions to win.
strategies: Start with lighthouses that have a count of 0 and mark their rows and columns as empty.
Look for overlapping paths between lighthouses with high numbers.

games.title: Lights Out
games.subtitle: Tap tiles to flip neighbours until all lights go out.
games.objective: Turn off all the lights on the grid. Tapping a light toggles its state and the state of adjacent lights.
games.controls: Tap a tile to toggle it and its immediate neighbors (up, down, left, right).
walkthrough: Step 1: Observe the initial pattern of lit and unlit tiles.
Step 2: Tap a tile to turn it off, noting how it flips its neighbors.
Step 3: Work your way across the grid to systematically turn off lights.
Step 4: Achieve a completely dark board to win.
strategies: Try solving row by row, turning off all lights in the current row by clicking the row below it.
Use patterns to solve the final row if you get stuck.

games.title: Lock Pattern
games.subtitle: Deduce the secret dot pattern from each clue.
games.objective: Memorize and recreate the displayed lock pattern by connecting the dots in the correct order.
games.controls: Drag your finger across the dots to draw the pattern.
walkthrough: Step 1: Watch the pattern being drawn on the grid.
Step 2: Memorize the exact sequence and direction.
Step 3: Swipe across the dots to recreate the sequence.
Step 4: Release your finger when the pattern is complete.
strategies: Break complex patterns down into simple geometric shapes.
Visualize a path or assign numbers to the dots to remember the order.

games.title: Logical Syllogisms
games.subtitle: Is the conclusion logically valid?
games.objective: Determine if a conclusion logically follows from the given premises.
games.controls: Tap 'Valid' or 'Invalid' based on your deduction.
walkthrough: Step 1: Read the provided statements carefully.
Step 2: Read the conclusion drawn from those statements.
Step 3: Decide if the conclusion is a guaranteed fact based ONLY on the statements.
Step 4: Tap the correct validity option.
strategies: Ignore real-world facts; base your answer only on the logic presented.
Draw Venn diagrams mentally to map out 'All', 'Some', or 'No' relationships.

games.title: Magnets
games.subtitle: Place magnets and blanks to match the border counts.
games.objective: Place domino-shaped magnets (with + and - poles) so they satisfy the row/column count constraints and identical poles do not touch.
games.controls: Tap cells to toggle between +, -, and empty.
walkthrough: Step 1: Check the numbers at the edges of the grid indicating how many + and - poles are in each row/column.
Step 2: Remember that + cannot touch + and - cannot touch - anywhere.
Step 3: Fill in the magnetic halves.
Step 4: Mark non-magnetic dominoes as blank to complete the grid.
strategies: Rows or columns with a count of 0 can immediately be filled with blanks.
If a domino must be magnetic, placing one pole forces the other.

games.title: Masyu Loop
games.subtitle: Draw a single loop matching Masyu circle rules.
games.objective: Draw a single non-intersecting loop passing through every circle. Pass straight through white circles and turn in adjacent cells; turn at 90° on black circles and go straight through adjacent cells.
games.controls: Tap and drag or tap adjacent dots to draw/erase loop segments.
walkthrough: Step 1: Check pearl positions; white pearls require a straight pass-through, black pearls require an immediate 90° corner.
Step 2: Connect adjacent nodes by tapping to build the path.
Step 3: Close the loop without branches or dead ends.
strategies: Black pearls near edges must turn inward.
White pearls along a wall must travel parallel to the border.

games.title: Mathrax
games.subtitle: Fill a Latin square obeying every corner rule.
games.objective: Fill every row and column with the numbers 1 to the side of the board, once each. The clue on each corner binds the four cells around it along both diagonals: E means all four are even, O means all odd, = means each diagonal pair is equal, and a number is the result of its operation on each diagonal pair.
games.controls: Tap a cell to write the next number, and keep tapping to cycle back to empty. The hint button writes one number the clues prove.
walkthrough: Step 1: The board is a Latin square before it is arithmetic. A number written in a cell is gone from the rest of its row and its column, and that alone fills a lot of a five by five.

Step 2: Read a corner clue as two separate questions. A +7 between four cells says the top left and the bottom right add to seven AND the top right and the bottom left add to seven. Either one failing breaks the clue.
Step 3: Use the small numbers first. A ×2 forces a 1 and a 2, a −1 forces two neighbours, and an E or an O decides the parity of four cells at once.
Step 4: When a row has only one cell left for a number, that cell is it, even if you have not looked at the corners yet.
Step 5: The board is finished when every row and column holds each number once and no corner is red. A number that repeats or a corner that fails shows in red.
strategies: Count the parity first: an E corner needs four even numbers, and on a five board that is 2 and 4 with one of them twice, so the corner immediately says which cells cannot hold 1, 3 or 5.
For a product clue, list the pairs that multiply to it before touching the board. A ×12 on a six board is 2 and 6 or 3 and 4, and which pair it is usually falls out of the row.
A × with the biggest number is the strongest clue on the board: it pairs the largest digit with a 1 or a 2, and there are very few places for either.

Division is the weakest of the four operations: a ÷2 means one number is twice the other, which is 1 and 2, 2 and 4, or 3 and 6 on a six board. List the pairs before you eliminate anything, and prefer a product clue when both are on the same corner.
Work from the corners inward. The four corner cells of the grid touch only one clue each, so they have the least to satisfy, and they feed the row and column rules for everything else.

games.title: Matrix Reasoning
games.subtitle: Complete the pattern in the 3x3 grid
games.objective: Identify the missing pattern in the visual matrix from the given choices.
games.controls: Tap the correct visual pattern from the options below the matrix.
walkthrough: Step 1: Observe the 3x3 grid of patterns with one missing piece.
Step 2: Find the logical rule governing the rows and columns (e.g., rotation, addition).
Step 3: Apply the rule to determine what the missing piece should look like.
Step 4: Tap the matching option to solve.
strategies: Test one feature at a time: first color, then shape, then rotation.
Verify your theory across both a row and a column to be sure.

games.title: Minesweeper
games.subtitle: Identify all the mines without triggering them.
games.objective: Clear the board without detonating any hidden mines, using numbered clues that indicate adjacent mines.
games.controls: Tap a tile to reveal it. Long-press to flag a suspected mine.
walkthrough: Step 1: Tap a random tile to open up a starting area.
Step 2: Look at the numbers; a '1' means exactly one mine is adjacent to it.
Step 3: Long-press to place a flag where you are certain a mine exists.
Step 4: Safely tap all non-mine tiles to complete the level.
strategies: If a '1' touches only one unrevealed tile, that tile MUST be a mine.
Once you've flagged the correct number of mines around a number, all its other adjacent tiles are safe.

games.title: Netslide
games.subtitle: Slide rows and columns until every pipe connects.
games.objective: Slide rows and columns until every pipe is joined to a pipe.
games.controls: Drag a tile one square along its row or column: the whole line slides round one step. Tiles never rotate. A wall across a line blocks it.
walkthrough: Step 1: Find the lines that cannot move. A wall stops its line, so those tiles are already where they will be.
Step 2: Slide a line that a misplaced tile sits in, and watch where the tile goes.
Step 3: Work pipe by pipe: join one pair, then keep that join out of the line you slide next.
Step 4: The board is won when every pipe meets a pipe.
strategies: A slide moves a whole line, so every tile in that line changes place at once. Count what moves with it.
Slides come in pairs: sliding the same line back restores the board.
Leave the line with the fewest tiles until last; it has the least room for mistakes.

games.title: Nonogram
games.subtitle: Reveal the hidden image using logic clues.
games.objective: Fill in a grid based on numerical clues to reveal a hidden pixel art picture.
games.controls: Tap a cell to fill it, tap again to mark it as empty (X), or long-press to drag.
walkthrough: Step 1: Look at the numbers at the beginning of each row and column. They indicate consecutive filled cells.
Step 2: Use intersecting clues to deduce which cells must be filled.
Step 3: Mark cells you know must be empty with an 'X' to narrow down possibilities.
Step 4: Continue deducing until the entire grid is correctly filled.
strategies: Start with the largest numbers, especially those that take up more than half the row/column.
Always mark empty spaces with an 'X' once you complete a clue block.
Never guess; every move should be based on pure logic.

games.title: Norinori
games.subtitle: Shade exactly two connected cells in each room.
games.objective: Shade exactly two cells in every defined region, ensuring no shaded cells touch diagonally or share borders in groups larger than two.
games.controls: Tap cells to toggle their shaded state, or mark them as definitively empty.
walkthrough: Step 1: Look at the grid divided into boldly outlined regions.
Step 2: Shade exactly two cells per region.
Step 3: Ensure that every shaded cell shares exactly one edge with another shaded cell (forming dominos).
Step 4: Ensure no domino touches another domino, not even diagonally.
strategies: If a region has only two cells, they must both be shaded.
Once you place a domino, surround it with empty marks since no other domino can touch it.
Use corner logic to deduce where dominos are forced to go.

games.title: Number Crossing
games.subtitle: Fit every listed number into the crossing slots.
games.objective: Lay every number in the list into the skeleton once, across or down, one digit per cell. A number that crosses another shares a cell with it, so both must have the same digit there, and the cells no number covers are wall.
games.controls: Tap a cell to write the next digit: 1, 2, up to 9, then empty again. Wall cells take nothing. The hint button writes what the crossings prove, which is sometimes a whole number at once.
walkthrough: Step 1: Count the strips. Every outlined strip takes exactly one number, and its length says which numbers fit it, so a three-cell strip can only hold a three-digit number.

Step 2: Read a crossing. The digit a strip needs at a crossing must be the digit the other strip needs there, so keep only the digits both strips allow. A crossing that leaves one digit has decided that cell.
Step 3: Write the digit. A decided digit rules out every number that would have written something else in that position, which is usually what collapses the next strip.

Step 4: Count on both sides. A number with only one strip left goes there; a strip with only one number left that fits takes it. Every strip is used and every number is placed, so the two counts are the same number.
Step 5: The board is done when every chip is struck through and no strip is red. A red strip is one that can no longer become a listed number.
strategies: Start with the threes. A three-digit number is far more specific than a two-digit one, so the strips it crosses usually fall first.
Use the list against itself. Two numbers that share their first two digits can only be told apart by the digit a crossing puts between them.
Watch a strip that crosses twice. One digit is a small clue, but a strip of three that meets two others has to satisfy both at once, and that often leaves exactly one number.
Never guess. Every board is dealt with exactly one filling, so a digit that feels like a guess is a crossing you have not used yet.

games.title: Number Path
games.subtitle: Place 1 to N so consecutive numbers touch.
games.objective: Place 1 to the last number on the grid, once each, so that every number touches the one before it and the one after it, along an edge or a corner.
games.controls: Tap an empty cell to write the next number. Tap a number you wrote to clear it. The hint button writes one number the printed clues prove.
walkthrough: Step 1: Find the 1. The cell that holds it touches the 2, so an isolated corner with one way in usually fixes its neighbour.
Step 2: Work from both ends. The lowest and highest printed numbers fix their own neighbours, and the walk closes in from the middle.
Step 3: A number only ever moves one cell, so a cell with eight neighbours can hold anything, and a corner cell can only hold numbers whose neighbours are near.
Step 4: When a printed number has only one free cell beside it, the number after it goes there. Write it; that closes one more door.
Step 5: The board is finished when every number is on it and every step touches the step before. A number out of reach shows in red.
strategies: Count room, not hope: if the next number has nowhere to go from a cell, that cell cannot hold this one.
A cell that touches only one empty cell is the end of the path from that side, which pins both of its neighbours.
Long printed runs already laid out are free deductions: every gap between two printed numbers is a mini path with fixed ends.
When the grid fills up, the last few numbers place themselves: the cells left are the numbers left, in order.

games.title: Nurikabe
games.subtitle: Build one connected sea around numbered islands.
games.objective: Create 'islands' of white cells containing exactly one number, surrounded by a continuous 'river' of black cells.
games.controls: Tap cells to mark them as black (river) or white (island).
walkthrough: Step 1: Look at the grid containing numbers. Each number is part of exactly one island of that exact size.
Step 2: Ensure all black cells form a single connected network.
Step 3: Ensure there are no 2x2 squares of black cells anywhere.
Step 4: Complete the grid by correctly defining all islands and the river.
strategies: A cell containing a '1' is its own island, so surround it entirely with black cells.
When two islands get too close, separate them with a wall of black cells.
If a block of black cells is about to form a 2x2 square, leave one cell white.

games.title: Path Finder
games.subtitle: Find the hidden path from S to E.
games.objective: Trace a continuous path of a specific length from the start point to the exit point without overlapping.
games.controls: Drag your finger across the grid to draw the path from start to finish.
walkthrough: Step 1: Identify the start (S) and exit (E) points on the grid.
Step 2: Note the required step length provided in the hint.
Step 3: Drag through the grid cells to create a path of the exact length.
Step 4: Connect the path to the exit point to complete the level.
strategies: If you reach the exit too early, you need to find a more winding route.
Keep track of the number of steps as you drag.
Work backwards from the exit to find valid path segments.

games.title: Pegs
games.subtitle: Jump pegs over neighbours until one peg remains.
games.objective: Clear the board until a single peg is left. Every jump captures the peg it hops over.
games.controls: Drag a peg onto the square it should land on. Or tap a peg to pick it up and tap the landing square. The hint button shows one jump.
walkthrough: Step 1: Look for a peg with an empty square exactly two cells away and a peg between them. That is a jump.
Step 2: Drag that peg onto the empty square. The peg it jumped over is removed.
Step 3: Keep jumping toward the edges. A peg stranded in a corner with no partner can never be captured.
Step 4: Finish when one peg remains.
strategies: Work from the outside in. The middle of the board is where you want your last peg, not where you want to start clearing.
Before a jump, check whether it leaves a peg isolated with no neighbour to jump over. That peg is dead weight you can never remove.
If two jumps look equally good, take the one that keeps the remaining pegs close together.

games.title: Pipes
games.subtitle: Connect matching colored dots with pipes.
games.objective: Rotate pipe segments to create a continuous, unbroken flow from the start point to the end point.
games.controls: Tap on individual pipe tiles to rotate them 90 degrees clockwise.
walkthrough: Step 1: Identify the start and end points of the pipeline.
Step 2: Tap pieces to align them towards adjacent tiles.
Step 3: Connect all segments ensuring there are no open, leaking ends.
Step 4: Complete the connection to let the fluid flow and finish the level.
strategies: Start from the edges or fixed points and work your way inwards.
Look for corners and straight pieces that can only fit in one logical way.
Avoid creating closed loops that don't connect to the main line.

games.title: Ripple Effect
games.subtitle: Fill regions 1..N; equal digits keep N cells apart.
games.objective: Fill every shape with the numbers 1 to its size, once each, so that two equal numbers in a line have at least that many cells between them.
games.controls: Tap a cell to select it, then tap a number to write it. Tap the same number again, or the eraser, to clear the cell. The hint button writes one number the clues prove.
walkthrough: Step 1: Look at the shapes, not at the numbers. A shape with four cells holds 1, 2, 3 and 4 exactly once.

Step 2: Read the ripple rule as a no-entry zone as wide as the number: a 1 keeps another 1 out of the four cells beside it, a 3 keeps another 3 out of the three cells either side, because two 3s need three cells between them.
Step 3: Count the room a number needs, not just the cells next to it. On a line of six cells a 3 in the second cell can only meet another 3 in the last, because it needs three cells of gap.
Step 4: When a shape has only one cell left that can hold a number, that cell is it. Write it and the ripple clears its neighbours.
Step 5: The board is finished when every cell holds a number and no digit sits too close to its twin. A number that breaks the ripple shows in red.
strategies: A 1 is the most useful clue on the board: it rules out its four orthogonal neighbours everywhere, and a shape of size one is simply that number.
Count the room a digit has along a line, not just beside it: two equal digits need one more cell of gap than the digit itself, so a 2 needs two cells between it and its twin and a 4 needs four.
Cross off by shape and by line at once: a digit placed in a shape is gone from that shape everywhere, even in cells far away.
The largest region's size is the highest digit on the board. Nothing above it exists, so a cell in a smaller shape can never take it.

games.title: Rome
games.subtitle: Point arrows so every path reaches a goal.
games.objective: Put one arrow in every cell. No arrow may repeat inside an outlined area, and if you follow the arrows from any cell you have to arrive at a circled goal, without ever looping or leaving the board.
games.controls: Tap a cell to cycle the four arrows and then blank. Printed arrows and circled goals are not yours to change. The hint button writes one arrow the rules prove.
walkthrough: Step 1: Read the edge first. A cell on the border has fewer than four arrows available, so the outside ring is decided before the middle.
Step 2: An outlined area may not hold the same arrow twice. Write an arrow and it is gone from the rest of its area, which on a four-cell area means each of the four appears exactly once.

Step 3: Follow chains that are already decided. If the cells a chain passes through are all written, you can see where it ends: at a goal, which is fine, or back where it started, which is the mistake.

Step 4: Ask where an arrow could end. An arrow whose chain can only run into a loop or into the edge is wrong, and that keeps an arrow pointing nowhere out of the cell even when you cannot see the whole chain.
Step 5: The board is finished when every cell holds an arrow, no arrow is red, and every chain reads its way to a circle.
strategies: Count the goals against the size of the board. Each goal only ends the chains that reach it, so on a board with few circles the arrows near a goal are the ones you can prove first.
Work the corners. A corner cell offers two arrows, one along each edge, and one of them often loops with its neighbour before anything else in the board is decided.

When two neighbouring cells both still allow only the arrows that point at each other, one of them has to go elsewhere. That pairing is the cheapest contradiction on a Rome board and it appears early.

Keep chains short. A cell whose arrow lands two steps from a goal is much easier to settle than one in the middle of a long run, so sort the cells you are unsure about by how far their chain has to travel.

games.title: Rule Finder
games.subtitle: Match each card by finding the hidden sorting rule.
games.objective: Deduce the hidden rule for sorting cards (by color, shape, or number) based on correctness feedback, and adapt when the rule changes.
games.controls: Tap one of the four piles to place your card.
walkthrough: Step 1: Look at the card to be sorted at the bottom.
Step 2: Place it on one of the four reference piles.
Step 3: Receive correctness feedback. Use this to identify if the current sorting rule is shape, color, or number.
Step 4: Adapt your sorting to follow this rule until it changes again.
strategies: Do not panic when a correct rule starts returning 'Incorrect' - it means the rule has shifted.
Always test rules systematically: color first, then shape, then number.
Remember the last correct rule to avoid repeating it immediately after a shift.

games.title: Salad
games.subtitle: Place each letter once per line; edges show first seen.
games.objective: Fill every row and column with the letters A to the last letter, once each, and leave the rest of each line as holes. Every letter printed around the border is the first one you meet looking into that line, skipping holes.
games.controls: Tap a cell to write the next value: a hole, then A, then B, up to the last letter, then back to a hole. The hint button writes one value the clues prove.
walkthrough: Step 1: Read the distance before the letter. A clue letter can only sit as many cells from its edge as the line has holes, so on a board with one hole per line the clue letter is in the first cell or the second.
Step 2: Everything in front of that point is a hole. Only holes can come before the clue letter, so the cell a clue points at is often decided before you look at anything else.
Step 3: A letter appears once in its row and once in its column. Write a letter and it is gone from the rest of its line, which is the same rule as a Latin square.
Step 4: Count what is left in a line. When a letter has only one cell left, it goes there; when a line already holds all its holes, every other cell is a letter.

Step 5: The board is finished when every line holds each letter once with the right number of holes and no clue is red. A clue turns red only when its line is decided and the first letter does not match.
strategies: Start at the edges, not the middle. The first cell of a line is either a hole or the clue letter and nothing else, which makes the border the most constrained part of the board.
Count holes before you count letters. Once both holes of a line are placed, every remaining cell is a letter, and the letters usually fall out of a single crossing with the line that meets it.
Use both ends of the same line. The clue on the left and the clue on the right bracket where the holes can be, and the cells that both clues leave free are where the interior has to sort itself out.
Write the hole when you are sure of it. A written hole eliminates nothing by itself, but it tightens the hole count of its line, and that is usually what turns the next letter into a single.

games.title: Same Game
games.subtitle: Clear groups of matching blocks to empty the board.
games.objective: Clear the board by removing groups of two or more squares of the same colour.
games.controls: Tap a group of two or more connected squares of the same colour to remove it. The squares above fall and the columns close up.
walkthrough: Step 1: Look for the colour that covers the most board and start there.
Step 2: Remove groups that join two other groups of the same colour once they fall together.
Step 3: Keep the small groups for last; they are the ones that strand single squares.
Step 4: The board is cleared when no group of two or more is left.
strategies: A single square can never be removed, so avoid cutting a group down to one.
Removing a tall group collapses the columns and can merge two groups that were apart.
Play from the bottom where you can: a collapse changes more of the board than a removal at the top.

games.title: Shikaku
games.subtitle: Divide the grid into rectangles matching each clue.
games.objective: Divide the grid into rectangles such that each contains exactly one number, and its area equals that number.
games.controls: Drag across the grid cells to draw rectangles.
walkthrough: Step 1: Look at the numbers scattered across the grid.
Step 2: Drag to create a rectangle around a number.
Step 3: Ensure the area of the rectangle matches the number exactly.
Step 4: Fill the entire grid with non-overlapping rectangles.
strategies: Start with large prime numbers, as they can only form 1xN or Nx1 rectangles.
Look for numbers trapped in corners or along the edges.
Use deduction: if a cell can only be reached by one specific number, include it in that rectangle.

games.title: Signpost
games.subtitle: Link cells in order by following their arrows.
games.objective: Number every cell from 1 to the last so that each cell points at the cell holding the next number.
games.controls: Drag a cell onto the cell it points at, or tap one cell and then the other. An arrow turns solid once its cell points somewhere; tapping that cell again takes the link back.
walkthrough: Step 1: Start from the given numbers. A given pins down the cell it sits in, and often the arrow into it.
Step 2: Follow each arrow as far as it can go along its line. The arrow runs along the whole ray, so the cell it means can be any distance away.
Step 3: An arrow that has only one cell left in its ray is decided for you: link it.
Step 4: Finish when one chain runs from 1 to the last number with every arrow pointing the way.
strategies: An arrow never points at a neighbour by default: it points at whatever lies along its line, so look to the end of the ray first.
Work backwards from the highest given number as well as forwards; both ends are constrained.
Every cell is used exactly once, so a number you cannot place in one ray is a reason to re-read the others.

games.title: Skyscrapers
games.subtitle: Place tower heights matching the edge sightlines.
games.objective: Place numbers 1 to N in the grid so no number repeats in any row or column, while satisfying the visibility clues.
games.controls: Tap a cell and select a number from the dial or pad.
walkthrough: Step 1: Look at the clues on the edges of the grid indicating how many 'skyscrapers' are visible.
Step 2: Taller numbers block smaller numbers behind them.
Step 3: Fill the grid such that each row and column has numbers 1-N without repeating.
Step 4: Ensure all edge clues are satisfied by the placed heights.
strategies: A clue of '1' means the tallest building (N) must be placed right next to it.
A clue of 'N' means the buildings must be in ascending order from that edge.
Use elimination similar to Sudoku for rows and columns.

games.title: Slitherlink
games.subtitle: Draw one closed loop matching the numbered cells.
games.objective: Connect adjacent dots to form a single continuous loop without crossings or branches.
games.controls: Tap the edges between dots to draw or remove a line.
walkthrough: Step 1: Look at the numbers inside the cells.
Step 2: The number indicates exactly how many of its 4 edges are part of the loop.
Step 3: Draw lines to satisfy all numbers.
Step 4: Ensure the lines form exactly one closed loop.
strategies: A '0' means no lines can surround it; mark them with 'x' to visually eliminate them.
Adjacent '3's always have parallel lines on their outer edges and a line between them.
The loop cannot branch or intersect itself, which helps logically force paths.

games.title: Sudoku
games.subtitle: Fill digits so each row, column, and box has all.
games.objective: Fill the 9x9 grid so that every row, column, and 3x3 box contains the digits 1 through 9 exactly once without any duplicates.
games.controls: Tap an empty cell on the grid to select it, then tap a number from the bottom keypad to fill it. Tap the selected cell again or the clear button to erase a number.
walkthrough: Step 1: Scan the grid for rows, columns, or 3x3 boxes that are almost full.
Step 2: Tap an empty cell in one of those areas.
Step 3: Determine the missing number and select it from the keypad.
Step 4: Repeat this process, using logic to deduce missing numbers until the entire grid is filled correctly.
strategies: Start with the 3x3 boxes that have the most given numbers.
Look for naked singles where only one specific number can possibly fit in a cell based on its row, column, and box.

games.title: Symbol Logic
games.subtitle: Find each symbol's value to solve the final line.
games.objective: Deduce the numerical value of different symbols based on a series of visual equations, then calculate and input the answer for the final question.
games.controls: Use the number pad to type your answer for the final equation. Tap the clear button to erase, and the checkmark button to submit your guess.
walkthrough: Step 1: Look at the first equation to determine the value of the first symbol (e.g., A + A = X).
Step 2: Use that value in the next equation to solve for the second symbol.
Step 3: Continue substituting known values to find the value of all symbols.
Step 4: Calculate the sum of the symbols in the final equation and enter the answer.
strategies: Always start with the equation that has two identical symbols.
Write down the values of the symbols if you have trouble keeping them in memory.

games.title: Tangle Fix
games.subtitle: Untangle the lines so none intersect
games.objective: Untangle the graph by moving the nodes so that none of the connecting lines cross each other.
games.controls: Tap and hold a node, then drag it around the screen to reposition it and untangle the connected lines.
walkthrough: Step 1: Look at the tangled web of nodes and intersecting lines.
Step 2: Identify lines that are crossing (highlighted in red).
Step 3: Drag the nodes connected to those lines to new positions.
Step 4: Continue repositioning nodes until all lines are clear and no longer intersect (turn green).
strategies: Try pulling nodes that have many connections towards the center, and nodes with few connections to the outside.
Look for triangles or loops of connected nodes and untangle them as a group.

games.title: Tapa
games.subtitle: Shade cells to form a continuous wall without 2x2 blocks.
games.objective: Paint a continuous black wall such that all clue numbers indicate consecutive wall blocks around each cell, with no 2x2 black squares.
games.controls: Tap an empty cell once to mark as wall, tap twice to mark with a red dot.
walkthrough: Step 1: Check numbered cells; each number indicates the length of consecutive shaded blocks surrounding it.
Step 2: Ensure all black wall cells form a single connected network.
Step 3: Never allow a 2x2 solid block of black wall cells.
strategies: Clue cells can never be shaded black.
A cell with '8' must be surrounded by 8 black cells.
Diagonal blocks separated by unshaded spaces fulfill multiple-number clues like (1, 1) or (1, 2).

games.title: Tenner Grid
games.subtitle: Fill rows with digits 0-9 matching column totals.
games.objective: Fill the grid so that each row contains the digits 0-9 exactly once, each column's sum matches the target number below it, and no adjacent cells (even diagonally) contain the same digit.
games.controls: Tap an empty cell on the grid to select it, then tap a number from the keypad below to fill it in.
walkthrough: Step 1: Tap an empty cell in the grid.
Step 2: Look at the column sum target and the other numbers in that column.
Step 3: Select a digit from the keypad that helps reach the sum without duplicating a number in the row or placing it next to an identical number.
Step 4: Fill the entire grid following all rules to win.
strategies: Start with columns that have high or low target sums, as they have fewer possible combinations.
Pay close attention to the rule that same numbers cannot touch diagonally.

games.title: Tents & Trees
games.subtitle: Pair each tree with a tent; tents never touch.
games.objective: Place tents in the grid so that every tree is paired with exactly one adjacent tent, no two tents touch each other (even diagonally), and the tent counts match the row and column clues.
games.controls: Tap an empty cell to place a tent, tap again to cycle to grass (empty), or tap again to clear.
walkthrough: Step 1: Look at the row and column clues indicating how many tents belong in each line.
Step 2: Find trees and tap adjacent empty cells to place tents next to them.
Step 3: Ensure no two tents touch each other, even diagonally.
Step 4: Complete the grid so all trees have a tent and all clues are satisfied.
strategies: Fill rows or columns with a '0' clue entirely with grass.
If a tree only has one valid empty space next to it, a tent must go there.

games.title: Tower of London
games.subtitle: Match the target configuration
games.objective: Move the colored beads between the three pegs to match the target configuration in the minimum number of moves, adhering to the height capacity of each peg.
games.controls: Tap a peg to select the top bead, then tap another peg to move the bead there.
walkthrough: Step 1: Compare the current layout of beads on the bottom pegs to the target configuration on the top pegs.
Step 2: Tap the peg holding the bead you want to move.
Step 3: Tap the destination peg to drop the bead, keeping in mind that the pegs can only hold 3, 2, and 1 beads respectively.
Step 4: Match the target configuration before running out of allowed moves.

games.title: Triplets Trio

games.title: Twiddle

A quarter turn moves four tiles at once, so prefer turns that fix two numbers rather than one.

games.title: Water Sort
games.subtitle: Sort the colors so each tube contains only one color.

Solve tubes containing colors that are already near the top first.
Plan your moves ahead to avoid locking yourself out of empty slots.

games.title: Yajilin

If a cell is shaded black, the loop must travel around it.

games.subtitle: Combine tiles with the same numbers to reach the 2048 tile.

games.title: Algebraic Balance

games.title: Angle Finder

Make small, fine adjustments using the slider before submitting your final answer.

games.title: Area & Perimeter
games.subtitle: Draw rectangles matching target area and perimeter values.

games.title: Balance Scale

Work methodically from the simplest scale to the most complex one.

games.title: Base Shift

Calculate carefully to avoid unnecessary steps.
Look for powers of 2, as they lead straight down to 1.

games.title: Common Denominator

Practice your multiplication tables to speed up calculation.

Check the operations; swapping numbers in a multiplication part changes the value drastically.

Ignore obvious wrong answers (e.g., odd numbers for an even divisor).
Focus on accuracy first, speed will follow.

games.title: Exponent Tower

Work systematically from smallest to largest.

games.subtitle: Solve sums and differences in Roman numerals.
